findings.message: T299: loadPack resolves every entry against registryUrls.get(kind), which loadRegistry overwrites on refresh. Reproduction: load the registry redirected to /v1/locales/index.json with resource ko-KR.json, then reload it redirected to /v2/locales/index.json with resource new/ko-KR.json. Both declared packs load successfully. Calling loadPack with the entry returned by the first registry now requests /v2/locales/ko-KR.json and fails with HTTP 404, although the original resource remains valid and cached. The URL combines an entry and base from different registry generations, violating resolution relative to the declaring JSON. Preserve the declaring registry URL with its entries, or otherwise resolve an entry and its base from the same registry generation. Add a regression covering a refresh that changes both the redirect base and relative resource path. Reproduced independently with injected fetch in /tmp/t299-review-registry-origin.mts.

findings.message: T301/T302: installThemeResources activates candidate resources and disposes the previous theme before this awaited call returns, but the controller only publishes the candidate after resuming and checking current() again at line 104. Registering a mounted image need in a completion observer before that await continuation invalidates needsRevision after the physical commit. The controller returns without publishing, then its automatic retry can fail loading the new scene. The pinned implementation finishes with snapshotTheme='pixel', installedTokens='candidate', pending=false and error=true: previous resources are already released while consumers still resolve the old pack. This violates the transactional/latest-request-wins requirement and ARCH-32's usable-selection preservation. Commit resource ownership and snapshot publication in one synchronous current-generation transaction, or restore the actual previous resources on invalidation; add a regression for this completion/needs-revision boundary followed by a failed retry. Reproduction: pnpm exec tsx /tmp/presentation-review-e6972811-transaction.mts. It uses the pinned controller and real installer with injected ports, prints the mismatch and fails the consistency assertion.

T301/T303: expect(registry.entries).toHaveLength(1) turns the current inventory into a permanent unit-suite constraint. In an isolated public tree, appending a conforming data-only-extension entry and matching cloned pack while retaining pixel as the default passes the actual validatePresentation function with both IDs. Running this exact, unmodified theme.test.ts against that tree then fails only this assertion (7 other cases pass). A resource-only theme addition therefore requires a TypeScript test edit to pass CI, contrary to ARCH-32 and T303's explicit prohibition on fixed supported-ID/one-entry assertions. Record this release's sole pixel inventory in the result/guide and validate shipped entries without restricting their count; retain extension coverage that accepts a second conforming resource without editing the shared test. Reproduction: pnpm exec tsx /tmp/presentation-review-e6972811-extension.mts; it preserves all repository files, validates the temporary two-theme tree, then runs the unchanged focused theme test there.
